newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee dips as state bank buys dollars.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee dips as state bank buys dollars.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee weakened in early trade on Tuesday after a state bank bought U.S. dollars, dealers said.
At 0430 GMT the rupee was trading at 56.75 against the dollar, down from the opening's 56.70 and against Monday's close at 56.72.
"The state bank is buying from where it left off yesterday," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by 2.25 local cents, and fixed buying and selling prices at 56.0687 and 57.2014.
Dealers said they did not expect the U.S. unit to rise above the 56.80-level as overall demand for the dollar was not high.
"Apart from a little genuine demand, all there is seems to be some short covering," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
Overnight call money was well-offered and trading at 13.5 percent, proving a disincentive to banks even doing currency swaps, he said.
